Header: Heteronychus arator African black beetle, Black maize beetle in English

Prevention: Deep plough to expose grubs to desiccation or birds and wait for 2-3 weeks before planting maize
Avoid planting maize close to tomato, potato or eggplants as these are host plants for beetles
Apply compost mixed with a biopesticide e.g.
Apply imidacloprid as a seed dressing before planting. (Refer to yellow direct control)
Rotate maize for two seasons with non- cereal crops such as legumes (soybeans) as these can reduce the population of the pest
Monitoring: Black oval shiny adult beetles, 1 to ½ cm long, usually migrate from breeding sites (swampy areas), to maize fields.
Grubs of the beetles are in the soil, and adult emerges from the soil after 4 months
Monitor the movement of adult beetles twice a week in the field, from
October, by installing 1 light trap, which contains water and soap per 100m² in maize field at night
Consider direct action when threshold for light trap catch is between 100-400 beetles per trap 100m2 per week, then refer to yellow control measure
Monitor plants more intensely during the first 3 weeks of planting, as beetle attack is rampant at this stage
Look for adults which chew the stem of newly germinated seedlings, resulting in death of plant
Take direct action when 2-5 beetles per root zone of plants are found.
Refer to yellow direct measure for control
Direct Control: Mass trap adult beetles using light traps hanged with a tripod or stick and container with water and soap, placed below to attract and kill migrating beetles. 1 to 2 traps per acre
Sprinkle ash on soil around root zone of young maize plant to repel beetles from attacking it
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
harvest intervals of pesticides in a certain crop must also be followed for the intercrop, and are sometimes even longer
